facts.claim: Cohen (1960) introduced kappa: the share of agreement between two judges after removing the agreement they would reach by chance.
Snow et al. (2008) found that, on an emotion-labelling task, an average of 4 non-expert labels per item matched the quality of one expert’s label.
In Snow et al.’s 2008 study, US$2.00 paid for 7,000 non-expert labels on Mechanical Turk.
Northcutt et al. (2021) estimated an average of at least 3.3% wrong labels across the test sets of 10 widely used datasets, and at least 6% in ImageNet’s validation set.
In uncertainty sampling, the learner asks for labels on the examples it is least certain how to label (Settles, Active Learning Literature Survey, 2009).
Gilardi et al. (2023) found ChatGPT’s zero-shot labels beat crowd workers’ accuracy on 4 of 5 text-labelling tasks, at under US$0.003 a label, about 20 times cheaper than Mechanical Turk.
